_comment: Editor UI metadata for FFT (First Fib Touch). Overlaid onto the schema built from FftConfig. UI ONLY — it never touches a trade decision. Click Scan Strategies after editing. There is no Pine file behind this strategy (1-minute bars cannot be exported from TradingView), so labels follow docs/FFT_SPEC.md's settings table rather than a Pine input panel. Descriptions are short and plain: what the setting does and what each choice means. The evidence behind each default lives in backtest/notes/fft_ledger.md.
edge: The first pullback into the 61.8 after the 5-minute trend turns, with the 15-minute trend behind it and the 1-minute still pulling back — bought or sold on the first touch and held to the 38.2.

steps.label: 01 · Trend
steps.title: 15m and 5m agree
steps.detail: The 15-minute trend and the 5-minute trend point the same way, and the 5-minute is on its first leg since it turned.

steps.label: 02 · Pullback
steps.title: The 1m pulls back against them
steps.detail: The 1-minute trend runs the other way and has not broken back in the trade's direction since the 5-minute leg's high or low.

steps.label: 03 · Touch
steps.title: First touch of the 61.8
steps.detail: A limit rests at the 61.8 of the 5-minute fib. Only the first touch of each leg counts; a leg that crosses a weekend is skipped.

steps.label: 04 · Exit
steps.title: Stop at the 1.0, target the 38.2
steps.detail: The stop sits at the start of the leg and the target at the 38.2. Nothing is moved in between.

tldr.text: Trades gold on 1-minute bars; the 5-minute and 15-minute are built from them.
Buys (or sells) the first touch of the 61.8 on the 5-minute's first leg, with the 15-minute trend behind it and the 1-minute pulling back.
Stop at the fib's 1.0, target the 38.2, one trade at a time.

params.name: size_mode
params.label: Position sizing
params.desc: Risk % of equity makes every trade the same size in risk terms. Fixed contracts uses the same quantity whatever the stop is.

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: ↳ Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks, measured from the 61.8 to the stop.

params.name: fixed_qty
params.label: ↳ Contracts
params.desc: The quantity used when sizing is set to fixed contracts.

params.name: max_bos
params.label: Max 5m continuation BOS
params.desc: How many times the 5-minute may have broken structure again since it turned. 0 is the first leg only; -1 allows any number.

params.name: req_15m
params.label: 15m trend must agree
params.desc: Only trade in the direction of the 15-minute trend.

params.name: skip_15m_overextended
params.label: Skip after 4+ 15m BOS
params.desc: Skip a setup when the 15-minute trend behind it has already broken structure 4 or more times since it turned. Off by default: these trades looked weaker in testing, but not by enough to prove it.

params.name: req_1m_against
params.label: 1m against, no 1m break
params.desc: The 1-minute trend must be running against the trade and must not have broken in the trade's direction since the leg's high or low.

params.name: skip_closure_legs
params.label: Skip a leg across a market closure
params.desc: Skip a setup whose leg crosses a weekend or holiday, and never leave the order resting into one.

params.name: stop_level
params.label: Stop level
params.desc: Where the stop sits on the 5-minute fib. 1.0 is the start of the leg; 88.6 is tighter.

params.name: target
params.label: Target
params.desc: Where the trade takes profit on the 5-minute fib. TP2 is further and pays more per trade; TP1 is hit more often.

params.name: second_touch
params.label: Trade the second touch when flat
params.desc: Also take the leg's second touch of the 61.8, once the first reached TP1 and no trade is open. Off: it is recorded but not traded.
